analysis.title: GS SECTOR SPECIALISTS: Energy, Natural Resources and Utilities Preview OFS Kick Off + Refining
key_insights: HAL reported headline revenue of $5.7bn vs Street $5.58bn. Adj EBITDA came in slightly below Street and EPS was broadly in line. D&E revenue beat and C&P revenue was below.

HAL's early 2027 outlook is mid-single digit revenue growth and operating margins of about 15%, roughly a 200 basis point improvement. The outlook assumes a flat North America market and no recovery in North America hydraulic fracturing, which HAL management calls purely upside. Street is at about 6% revenue growth and about 15% margins.
GS views the bar for HAL as relatively low this quarter. Positioning over the last couple of weeks is cleaner than last quarter and through conference season, and the desk positioning score is 5/10.

The HAL guide on the 9 AM ET call will likely drive price action and read-through for the oilfield services (OFS) group, with a heavy number of OFS prints over the next several days. North America expectations for HAL are low.

GS says crude price is not the force for services stocks (dated Brent at $117/b), and MOU, collaboration and contract headlines have not helped much. GS thinks the services group needs a reset of numbers plus a number of ways to win.
WFRD is the next services company to report EPS (post close on the day of the note). HAL commentary on LATAM, Africa and Middle East is expected to read through to WFRD to some extent.

Refining: VLO reports Thursday pre-market as the bellwether print this week, and GS says expectations for the group are extremely high. Cracks have come off but remain well above seasonal averages, and the seasonal roll question has become more topical on the desk.

WCS remains wide and continues to price at a steep discount, though Brent/WTI has narrowed a bit. GS says the desk was more willing to fight the move higher over the last couple of months, and specialists are now more neutral on the group while looking for reasons to fade strength.

GS expects 3Q refining EPS to be extremely strong, with VLO potentially at $25 EPS this quarter. GS has more concern about leading-edge consensus numbers for coming quarters drifting lower given recent crack moves.

GS expects less focus on buybacks in refining prints and sees potential for capital spend to surprise to the upside on secondary unit projects. With cracks where they are and views on mid cycle, payback period on those projects is not a big concern.
